title: Predictara Concept Intelligence Graph (CIG) - NCERT Class 6 Mathematics with Cross-Chapter, Cross-Class & Multidisciplinary Foundations
curriculum: NCERT Ganita Prakash (Grade 6) + Prior Grade Foundations (Grades 4-5) + Cross-Disciplinary STEM Links

concept.name: Mathematics as pattern-finding
concept.description: Recognise that mathematics involves identifying patterns and explaining why they occur.

concept.name: Number sequences
concept.description: Recognise an ordered sequence of numbers and describe a rule that generates it.

concept.name: Counting numbers
concept.description: Identify and extend the counting-number sequence.

concept.name: Odd numbers
concept.description: Identify odd numbers and extend the sequence using a consistent rule.

concept.name: Even numbers
concept.description: Identify even numbers and extend the sequence using a consistent rule.

concept.name: All-ones sequence
concept.description: Recognise the constant sequence 1, 1, 1, … and reason about repeated addition.

concept.name: Triangular numbers
concept.description: Recognise triangular numbers through dot arrangements and numeric sequences.

concept.name: Square numbers
concept.description: Recognise square numbers through square arrays and numeric sequences.

concept.name: Cube numbers
concept.description: Recognise cube numbers and connect them to three-dimensional arrangements.

concept.name: Virahanka numbers
concept.description: Recognise the sequence in which each term after the first two is formed from the previous two.

concept.name: Powers of 2
concept.description: Recognise and extend a sequence formed by repeated multiplication by 2.

concept.name: Powers of 3
concept.description: Recognise and extend a sequence formed by repeated multiplication by 3.

concept.name: Visualising number sequences
concept.description: Represent numeric sequences with dots, arrays or other pictures.

concept.name: Hexagonal numbers
concept.description: Recognise and extend the illustrated hexagonal-number pattern.

concept.name: Relations among number sequences
concept.description: Explore relationships between sequences and explain them using numerical or visual reasoning.

concept.name: Odd-number sums and square numbers
concept.description: Recognise and explain the pattern that successive odd-number sums form square numbers.

concept.name: Ascending and descending counting sums
concept.description: Explore the chapter's up-and-down counting-sum pattern that produces square numbers.

concept.name: Shape sequences
concept.description: Identify, continue and describe a rule for a sequence of shapes.

concept.name: Regular polygons
concept.description: Recognise the sequence of regular polygons by increasing side and corner counts.

concept.name: Complete graphs
concept.description: Explore the chapter's sequence of complete graphs and count connecting lines.

concept.name: Stacked squares
concept.description: Explore the stacked-squares pattern and relate the number of small squares to a number sequence.

concept.name: Stacked triangles
concept.description: Explore the stacked-triangles pattern and relate the number of small triangles to a number sequence.

concept.name: Koch snowflake iterations
concept.description: Recognise the iterative shape pattern and count line segments across stages.

concept.name: Connecting shape and number sequences
concept.description: Count sides, corners, lines or component shapes and map these counts to number sequences.

concept.name: Point as location
concept.description: Recognise a point as a dimensionless location in space, denoted by a single capital letter.

concept.name: Line segment
concept.description: Identify a line segment as the shortest path between two points with two fixed endpoints and measurable length.

concept.name: Line
concept.description: Recognise a line as a straight path extending indefinitely in two opposite directions with no endpoints.

concept.name: Ray
concept.description: Identify a ray as a straight path starting at an initial point (origin/vertex) and extending infinitely in one direction.

concept.name: Collinear points
concept.description: Identify three or more points lying on the same straight line.

concept.name: Intersecting lines
concept.description: Identify pairs of lines that cross each other at exactly one common point.

concept.name: Parallel lines
concept.description: Recognise coplanar lines that maintain equal perpendicular distance and never intersect no matter how far extended.

concept.name: Perpendicular lines
concept.description: Identify pairs of lines or segments that meet or intersect at a right angle (90 degrees).

concept.name: Angle definition and components
concept.description: Recognise an angle as formed by two rays meeting at a common vertex; identify arms and vertex.

concept.name: Interior and exterior of an angle
concept.description: Distinguish regions inside (interior) versus outside (exterior) of an angle in the plane.

concept.name: Rotation model of angles
concept.description: Understand an angle as an amount of turn or rotation of an arm about a fixed pivot.

concept.name: Comparing angles by superimposition
concept.description: Compare angles by visual inspection, tracing, or overlaying arms rather than by length of drawn arms.

concept.name: Right angle
concept.description: Identify a right angle as a quarter-turn rotation (90 degrees), equivalent to the corner of a square.

concept.name: Straight angle
concept.description: Identify a straight angle as a half-turn rotation (180 degrees), forming a straight line.

concept.name: Complete angle and zero angle
concept.description: Identify complete angle as full 360-degree rotation and zero angle as no rotation.

concept.name: Acute angles
concept.description: Classify angles strictly between 0 degrees and 90 degrees.

concept.name: Obtuse angles
concept.description: Classify angles strictly between 90 degrees and 180 degrees.

concept.name: Reflex angles
concept.description: Classify angles strictly between 180 degrees and 360 degrees.

concept.name: Measuring angles with protractor
concept.description: Measure angles accurately in degrees (0 to 180) using inner and outer scales of a protractor.

concept.name: Drawing angles to given measure
concept.description: Construct angles of specific degree measures using protractor, ruler, and pencil.

concept.name: Large numbers and Indian/International place value
concept.description: Read, write and compare numbers up to crores and millions with appropriate commas.

concept.name: Supercells and base-10 powers
concept.description: Decompose numbers into base-10 powers and expanded notation.

concept.name: Number line intervals and scale
concept.description: Locate large numbers on number lines with uniform intervals; compute distances as differences.

concept.name: Digit permutation and extreme numbers
concept.description: Form the greatest and smallest numbers from given digits with and without repetition.

concept.name: Palindromic numbers
concept.description: Identify numbers that read the same backwards and forwards; explore reverse-and-add patterns.

concept.name: Kaprekar routine
concept.description: Execute Kaprekar algorithm on 3-digit (495) and 4-digit (6174) numbers.

concept.name: Modular clock and calendar arithmetic
concept.description: Recognise cyclic patterns in clocks (mod 12, mod 24) and calendars (mod 7).

concept.name: Mental math compensation strategies
concept.description: Use friendly numbers (making tens, making hundreds, compensation like +99 = +100 - 1).

concept.name: Multiplication patterns by 9 and 11
concept.description: Apply shortcuts and pattern rules for multiplying by 9, 11, and computing digital roots.

concept.name: Collatz sequence (3n+1)
concept.description: Iterate the 3n+1 rule (half if even, 3n+1 if odd) and observe trajectory convergence.

concept.name: Rounding off and estimation
concept.description: Round numbers to nearest 10, 100, 1000 using midpoint rule.

concept.name: Estimation of operations
concept.description: Estimate sums, differences, products, and quotients to evaluate calculation reasonableness.

concept.name: Mathematical games and winning strategies
concept.description: Analyze turn-based arithmetic games using backwards induction and invariant states.

concept.name: Data collection and recording
concept.description: Collect observational or survey data and record raw records systematically.

concept.name: Tally marks and frequency counts
concept.description: Organise raw data using bundles of five tally marks and frequency columns.

concept.name: Frequency distribution table
concept.description: Construct structured tables summarizing categories and associated counts.

concept.name: Concept of a pictograph
concept.description: Represent numerical data visually using scaled symbols or pictures.

concept.name: Scale and key in pictographs
concept.description: Establish and interpret symbol multipliers (e.g. 1 icon = 10 units, half icon = 5 units).

concept.name: Interpreting pictographs
concept.description: Extract frequencies, compare categories, and compute totals and differences from pictographs.

concept.name: Constructing pictographs
concept.description: Draw icons accurately according to chosen scale, including fractional symbols.

concept.name: Concept of a bar graph
concept.description: Represent categorical frequencies as rectangular bars of uniform width and proportional height.

concept.name: Axis labeling and bar spacing
concept.description: Label category and numerical axes clearly; maintain uniform width and equal gap between bars.

concept.name: Scale selection on bar graphs
concept.description: Determine appropriate scale increments (1 unit = 1, 2, 5, 10, 50, 100) based on data range.

concept.name: Interpreting vertical and horizontal bar graphs
concept.description: Read bar heights/lengths against axis markings to answer analytical queries.

concept.name: Constructing bar graphs
concept.description: Plot bars accurately on grid/graph paper with descriptive titles and scale markings.

concept.name: Comparative and critical data analysis
concept.description: Identify modal categories, interpret trends, and detect misleading graph representations.

concept.name: Factors of a number
concept.description: Identify exact divisors of a number; recognize 1 and number itself as factors.

concept.name: Multiples of a number
concept.description: Generate multiples by multiplying a number by counting integers (1, 2, 3...).

concept.name: Common factors
concept.description: Find factors shared by two or more numbers.

concept.name: Highest Common Factor (HCF/GCD)
concept.description: Determine the greatest factor common to given numbers.

concept.name: Common multiples
concept.description: Identify multiples shared by two or more numbers.

concept.name: Lowest Common Multiple (LCM)
concept.description: Determine the smallest non-zero multiple common to given numbers.

concept.name: Prime vs composite numbers
concept.description: Distinguish numbers with exactly two distinct factors (prime) from those with more than two (composite).

concept.name: Properties of 1 and 2
concept.description: Understand 1 is neither prime nor composite; 2 is the smallest prime and only even prime.

concept.name: Sieve of Eratosthenes
concept.description: Apply systematic cancellation of composite multiples to discover primes up to 100.

concept.name: Twin primes
concept.description: Identify pairs of prime numbers that differ by exactly 2 (e.g., 3 and 5, 11 and 13).

concept.name: Co-prime numbers
concept.description: Identify pairs of numbers whose HCF is 1, recognizing numbers need not be prime themselves.

concept.name: Prime factorisation
concept.description: Express composite numbers uniquely as products of prime factors.

concept.name: Factor tree representation
concept.description: Construct branching factor trees to decompose numbers into prime leaves.

concept.name: Continuous division for prime factorisation
concept.description: Apply ladder division method using smallest prime divisors.

concept.name: HCF by prime factorisation
concept.description: Compute HCF using product of common prime factors with smallest powers.

concept.name: LCM by prime factorisation
concept.description: Compute LCM using product of all prime factors with highest powers.

concept.name: Divisibility rules for 2, 5, 10
concept.description: Determine divisibility using last digit checks.

concept.name: Divisibility rules for 3 and 9
concept.description: Determine divisibility using digital sum test and understand mathematical justification.

concept.name: Divisibility rules for 4 and 8
concept.description: Determine divisibility using last 2 and last 3 digit inspection.

concept.name: Divisibility rule for 11
concept.description: Determine divisibility using alternating sum of digits difference test.

concept.name: Concept of perimeter
concept.description: Understand perimeter as the total distance around the closed boundary of a 2D planar figure (1D length).

concept.name: Perimeter by direct side summation
concept.description: Calculate perimeter by adding the lengths of all outer boundary segments.

concept.name: Perimeter of a rectangle
concept.description: Apply formula P = 2 * (length + breadth) derived from pair-wise equality of opposite sides.

concept.name: Perimeter of a square
concept.description: Apply formula P = 4 * side for equilateral quadrilaterals.

concept.name: Perimeter of regular polygons
concept.description: Apply formula P = n * side for equilateral triangles, pentagons, and hexagons.

concept.name: Perimeter of composite rectilinear figures
concept.description: Trace outer perimeter of compound L-shaped and T-shaped figures without counting internal edges.

concept.name: Concept of area
concept.description: Understand area as the measure of planar surface enclosed inside a closed boundary (2D region in square units).

concept.name: Standard units of area
concept.description: Use square centimeter (cm^2) and square meter (m^2) as standard tiled measurement units.

concept.name: Area estimation by grid counting
concept.description: Count unit squares on squared grid paper: full squares, half squares (count 1/2), ignore < 1/2 squares.

concept.name: Area of a rectangle
concept.description: Apply formula Area = length * breadth derived from tiling arrays of unit squares.

concept.name: Area of a square
concept.description: Apply formula Area = side * side = s^2.

concept.name: Area of compound rectilinear figures
concept.description: Decompose irregular shapes into non-overlapping rectangles and sum component areas.

concept.name: Area of a right-angled triangle
concept.description: Decompose a rectangle into two congruent triangles: Area = 1/2 * base * height.

concept.name: Area of a general triangle
concept.description: Compute triangle area as half of enclosing rectangle/parallelogram: Area = 1/2 * b * h.

concept.name: Independence of perimeter and area
concept.description: Recognise that shapes with identical perimeter can have different areas, and vice versa.

concept.name: Applied contextual perimeter vs area problems
concept.description: Distinguish perimeter contexts (fencing, borders, ribbons) from area contexts (tiling, turfing, painting).

concept.name: Fractional units and equal shares
concept.description: Understand a fraction as dividing a whole quantity into n equal parts; unit fraction 1/n.

concept.name: Fraction as part of a whole
concept.description: Interpret numerator as count of parts and denominator as total equal parts in the whole.

concept.name: Fractions of a collection/set
concept.description: Determine fractional parts of a discrete set of objects (e.g. 2/3 of 12 items).

concept.name: Proper fractions
concept.description: Identify fractions strictly less than 1, where numerator < denominator.

concept.name: Improper fractions
concept.description: Identify fractions representing 1 or more wholes, where numerator >= denominator.

concept.name: Mixed fractions
concept.description: Express improper fractions as whole number + proper fraction.

concept.name: Converting between mixed and improper fractions
concept.description: Fluently convert between mixed numbers (w a/b) and improper fractions ((w*b + a)/b).

concept.name: Fractions on the number line
concept.description: Subdivide unit intervals [0, 1] and [1, 2] into equal denominator segments to plot fractions.

concept.name: Concept of equivalent fractions
concept.description: Recognise that distinct fractional representations express the identical quantity or number line position.

concept.name: Generating equivalent fractions by scaling
concept.description: Multiply or divide numerator and denominator by the exact same non-zero factor k.

concept.name: Simplest form / lowest terms
concept.description: Divide numerator and denominator by their HCF until numerator and denominator are co-prime.

concept.name: Comparing like fractions
concept.description: Compare fractions sharing identical denominators by directly comparing numerators.

concept.name: Comparing fractions with like numerators
concept.description: Understand inverse denominator size: larger denominator divides whole into smaller pieces.

concept.name: Comparing unlike fractions
concept.description: Compare fractions with different denominators by converting to common denominator or cross-multiplication.

concept.name: Addition of like fractions
concept.description: Add numerators while maintaining the common denominator: a/d + b/d = (a+b)/d.

concept.name: Subtraction of like fractions
concept.description: Subtract numerators while keeping common denominator unchanged.

concept.name: Addition of unlike fractions via LCM
concept.description: Determine LCM of denominators, scale to equivalent fractions, and sum numerators.

concept.name: Subtraction of unlike fractions via LCM
concept.description: Determine LCM of denominators, scale to equivalent fractions, and subtract numerators.

concept.name: Addition and subtraction of mixed fractions
concept.description: Add and subtract mixed numbers by combining whole and fractional parts or converting to improper fractions.

concept.name: Multi-step fraction word problems
concept.description: Translate real-world sharing, measurement, and comparison scenarios into fractional operations.

concept.name: Geometrical drawing tools
concept.description: Use ruler, compass, divider, protractor, and set-squares effectively and safely.

concept.name: Circle and circular arcs
concept.description: Define circle, center, radius, diameter (d=2r), and chord; draw circles of given radius with compass.

concept.name: Constructing a line segment of given length
concept.description: Use ruler and compass to measure and construct line segments of specific length.

concept.name: Copying a given line segment
concept.description: Replicate an existing segment length using compass span without measuring with ruler numbers.

concept.name: Geometric properties of rectangles and squares
concept.description: Identify equal opposite sides, four right angles, and parallel side pairs.

concept.name: Constructing rectangles of given dimensions
concept.description: Construct rectangles of given length and breadth using set-squares, protractor, and straightedge.

concept.name: Constructing squares of given side
concept.description: Construct squares using compass and perpendicular lines.

concept.name: Equality of rectangle diagonals
concept.description: Verify and prove that the two diagonals of a rectangle and square are strictly equal in length.

concept.name: Mutual bisection of diagonals
concept.description: Verify that diagonals of rectangles and squares bisect each other at their common midpoint.

concept.name: Perpendicularity of square diagonals
concept.description: Verify that diagonals of a square are both equal in length and mutually perpendicular (intersect at 90 degrees).

concept.name: Perpendicular to a line through a given point
concept.description: Construct perpendicular lines using set-squares and compass from a point on or outside a line.

concept.name: Points equidistant from two given points
concept.description: Explore the set of points equidistant from two fixed endpoints; introduce perpendicular bisector locus.

concept.name: Constructing the perpendicular bisector of a segment
concept.description: Draw intersecting circular arcs from two endpoints to construct the perpendicular bisector line.

concept.name: Constructing angle bisectors
concept.description: Construct the ray dividing a given angle into two congruent angles using compass arcs.

concept.name: Constructing standard angles (60, 90, 120 degrees)
concept.description: Construct fundamental angles using straightedge and compass alone without protractor.

concept.name: Concept of symmetry and visual balance
concept.description: Identify symmetry as balanced and identical proportions across nature, architecture, and geometry.

concept.name: Line of symmetry (reflection axis)
concept.description: Identify an imaginary line dividing a shape into two congruent halves that coincide under folding.

concept.name: Mirror line and reflection verification
concept.description: Verify reflectional symmetry using paper folding or mirror line placement.

concept.name: Figures with a single line of symmetry
concept.description: Identify shapes with exactly one line of symmetry (e.g. isosceles triangle, kite, letters A, M, V).

concept.name: Figures with two lines of symmetry
concept.description: Identify shapes with exactly two orthogonal lines of symmetry (e.g. rectangle, rhombus, letters H, I, X).

concept.name: Figures with multiple lines of symmetry
concept.description: Identify shapes with 3, 4, 5, 6 lines of symmetry (equilateral triangle, square, regular pentagon, regular hexagon).

concept.name: Infinite lines of symmetry in a circle
concept.description: Recognise that every diameter passing through the center of a circle is a line of symmetry.

concept.name: Completing symmetrical figures
concept.description: Draw the reflected half of an incomplete planar figure across a given line of symmetry.

concept.name: Concept of rotational symmetry
concept.description: Recognise when a figure looks identical to its initial state after a turn about a fixed point.

concept.name: Center of rotation
concept.description: Identify the fixed pivot point around which rotational symmetry occurs.

concept.name: Angle of rotation
concept.description: Determine the minimum positive angle of turn needed for a shape to map onto itself.

concept.name: Order of rotational symmetry
concept.description: Determine the number of times a figure matches its initial orientation during a full 360-degree rotation.

concept.name: Shapes with both reflectional and rotational symmetry
concept.description: Analyze shapes exhibiting dual symmetry (e.g. square: 4 reflection lines, rotational order 4).

concept.name: Need for numbers beyond zero
concept.description: Recognise practical situations requiring negative quantities: sub-zero temperatures, basement depths, debts, sea levels.

concept.name: Bela building of fun elevator model
concept.description: Model positive integers as upper floors (+1, +2...), ground floor as 0, and basements as negative floors (-1, -2...).

concept.name: The set of integers
concept.description: Define integers as the set containing negative integers, zero, and positive integers (Z = {... -3, -2, -1, 0, 1, 2, 3...}).

concept.name: Zero as the neutral reference point
concept.description: Understand zero is neither positive nor negative; acts as neutral origin.

concept.name: Number line representation of integers
concept.description: Plot positive integers to the right of zero and negative integers to the left of zero with uniform intervals.

concept.name: Opposite / additive inverse
concept.description: Identify opposite integers equidistant from 0 on the number line; a + (-a) = 0.

concept.name: Ordering and comparing integers
concept.description: Compare integers on a horizontal number line: numbers to the right are always greater (-2 > -8).

concept.name: Token model of integers
concept.description: Represent integers using positive counters (+1) and negative counters (-1).

concept.name: Zero pair concept
concept.description: Understand that one positive token and one negative token cancel each other out to make zero: (+1) + (-1) = 0.

concept.name: Integer addition with like signs
concept.description: Add numbers with identical signs by summing magnitudes and retaining common sign: (-3) + (-5) = -8.

concept.name: Integer addition with unlike signs
concept.description: Add numbers with opposite signs by computing difference of magnitudes and assigning sign of larger magnitude.

concept.name: Integer addition on the number line
concept.description: Model addition by starting at first integer and moving right for positive addend or left for negative addend.

concept.name: Integer subtraction as adding the opposite
concept.description: Transform subtraction into addition of additive inverse: a - b = a + (-b).

concept.name: Subtraction on the token model
concept.description: Remove tokens or introduce zero pairs to subtract negative and positive quantities.

concept.name: Double negative concept (minus minus is plus)
concept.description: Understand why subtracting a negative integer increases value: a - (-b) = a + b.

concept.name: Integer subtraction on the number line
concept.description: Model subtraction by moving in the direction opposite to addition.

concept.name: Successor and predecessor in integers
concept.description: Determine successor (n+1) and predecessor (n-1) of negative integers (e.g. successor of -5 is -4, predecessor is -6).

concept.name: Applied multi-step integer problems
concept.description: Solve contextual elevation, temperature change, and financial balance problems.

concept.name: Whole Number Place Value to 10,000 (Class 5)
concept.description: Understand periods (ones, thousands) and place value up to 5-digit numbers; foundational prior grade prerequisite.

concept.name: Multiplication Tables 1-12 Fluency (Class 5)
concept.description: Rapid procedural recall of single-digit multiplication facts; critical prerequisite for factors, multiples and fractions.

concept.name: Division as Equal Sharing and Grouping (Class 5)
concept.description: Understand division as sharing equally and forming groups with quotient and remainder.

concept.name: Fraction Intuition: Half, Quarter, Three-Quarters (Class 5)
concept.description: Concrete visual recognition of 1/2, 1/4, 3/4 on circular cakes, paper strips and collections.

concept.name: Basic 2D Closed Shapes (Class 5)
concept.description: Identify and distinguish triangles, rectangles, squares and circles by side and vertex counts.

concept.name: Length Measurement in cm and m (Class 5)
concept.description: Measure real objects using 15 cm and 30 cm rulers; align 0-mark accurately to object edge.

concept.name: Reading Simple Pictographs (Class 5)
concept.description: Interpret icons representing multiple units (e.g. 1 star = 5 books) in visual data tables.

concept.name: Multi-digit Addition & Subtraction with Regrouping (Class 4)
concept.description: Column addition and borrowing/regrouping across place value positions.

concept.name: Skip Counting Sequences by 2, 3, 5, 10 (Class 4)
concept.description: Verbal and written forward skip counting forming the cognitive bridge to multiplication tables and patterns.

concept.name: Identifying Straight vs Curved Lines (Class 4)
concept.description: Differentiate between straight ruler edges and curved boundaries in natural and geometric shapes.

concept.name: Thermometers & Sub-Zero Temperatures (Science / Physics)
concept.description: Science Link: The Celsius thermometer scale with 0°C freezing point of water and negative numbers representing sub-zero temperatures (Himalayas, Arctic).
concept.subject: Science

concept.name: Sea Level Datum, Elevation & Depth (Geography / Earth Science)
concept.description: Geography Link: Mean sea level as 0 meter benchmark; positive integers represent mountain altitude (+8848m Mt Everest), negative integers represent ocean depths (-11000m Mariana Trench).
concept.subject: Geography

concept.name: Meteorological Data, Rainfall & Temperature Charts (Science / EVS)
concept.description: Science Link: Tracking daily rainfall using rain gauges, recording weather tallies, and plotting monthly temperature curves using bar graphs.
concept.subject: Science

concept.name: Biological Symmetry in Flora & Fauna (Biology / Life Science)
concept.description: Biology Link: Bilateral symmetry in butterflies, human face and leaves; radial symmetry in hibiscus flowers, starfish and honeycomb hex patterns.
concept.subject: Biology

concept.name: Solution Concentrations & Dilution Ratios (Science / Chemistry)
concept.description: Chemistry Link: Solute-solvent proportions, 1/4 dilution, saline water concentration and parts of chemical mixtures expressed as rational fractions.
concept.subject: Science

concept.name: Directional Bearings, Navigation & Shadow Angles (Physics / Astronomy)
concept.description: Physics Link: Compass rose 8-point bearings (90° North-to-East quarter turns); solar angle of elevation determining shadow length on sundials.
concept.subject: Physics

concept.name: Tessellations, Rangoli & Architectural Motifs (Art / Architecture)
concept.description: Art Link: Geometric tile tessellations without gaps, symmetrical Indian Rangoli/Kolam floor art, and repetitive polygonal Islamic architectural friezes.
concept.subject: Art

edge.name: LCM Prerequisite for Unlike Fraction Addition
edge.description: Finding LCM of denominators in Chapter 5 is a strict blocking prerequisite for adding unlike fractions in Chapter 7.

edge.name: LCM Prerequisite for Unlike Fraction Subtraction
edge.description: Finding common multiple/LCM in Chapter 5 is mandatory before subtracting fractions with differing denominators in Chapter 7.

edge.name: HCF Prerequisite for Fraction Simplification
edge.description: Finding Highest Common Factor (HCF) in Chapter 5 is the mathematical prerequisite for reducing fractions to simplest form.

edge.name: Common Factors Support Equivalent Fractions
edge.description: Factorization insight supports understanding why multiplying/dividing numerator and denominator by same factor preserves value.

edge.name: Multiples Concept Supports Fraction Scaling
edge.description: Generating multiples of a number provides the procedural foundation for generating equivalent fraction chains.

edge.name: Line Segment Measurement Prerequisite for Ruler/Compass Construction
edge.description: Accurate line segment definition and measurement in Ch 2 is prerequisite for constructing line segments in Ch 8.

edge.name: Angle Vertex/Arms Prerequisite for Angle Construction
edge.description: Understanding vertex, arms and rotational degree measure in Ch 2 is prerequisite for constructing 60°, 90°, 120° angles in Ch 8.

edge.name: Perpendicular Lines Prerequisite for Perpendicular Bisector
edge.description: Knowing that perpendiculars form 90° angles is prerequisite for constructing perpendicular bisector using compass.

edge.name: Angle Types Support Angle Bisector Construction
edge.description: Classifying acute/obtuse angles supports verifying that bisector divides angle into two equal acute halves.

edge.name: Boundary Segments Prerequisite for Perimeter
edge.description: Understanding closed polygonal boundaries composed of line segments is prerequisite for perimeter.

edge.name: Right Angles Support Rectangle Area
edge.description: Perpendicular adjacent sides (90°) in rectangles enable partitioning into a grid of unit squares (l x b).

edge.name: Regular Polygons Support Line Symmetry Analysis
edge.description: Recognizing n-sided regular polygons from Ch 1 allows learners to deduce that an n-gon possesses exactly n lines of symmetry in Ch 9.

edge.name: Sequence Rules Support Rotational Symmetry Orders
edge.description: Mathematical sequence rules support calculating rotational symmetry angle intervals (360/n).

edge.name: Square Numbers Structural Analog of Square Area
edge.description: Dot arrays for square numbers (n^2) from Ch 1 are structurally identical to the unit square tiling area formula in Ch 6.

edge.name: Multiplication Prerequisite for Rectangle Area Formula
edge.description: Fluent 2-digit by 2-digit multiplication from Ch 3 is mandatory for applying Area = Length x Breadth.

edge.name: Division with Remainder Prerequisite for Divisibility & Factors
edge.description: Zero remainder upon division from Ch 3 is the mathematical definition of a factor in Ch 5.

edge.name: Large Number Estimation Supports Bar Graph Scaling
edge.description: Rounding and place-value estimation from Ch 3 helps students choose intervals (e.g. 1 unit = 100 students) in Ch 4.

edge.name: Bar Graph Proportions Support Fraction Part-to-Whole Intuition
edge.description: Visualizing relative heights on bar charts reinforces fraction as proportion of a total quantity.

edge.name: Fraction Number Line Structural Analog of Integer Number Line
edge.description: Locating fractions between 0 and 1 transfers directly to calibrating negative numbers to the left of 0.

edge.name: Fraction Comparison Supports Integer Ordering
edge.description: Position-based ordering on the horizontal line supports understanding why -5 < -2.

edge.name: Addition Hops on Number Line Transfers to Integer Addition
edge.description: Vector hop model of fraction addition supports directed movement (right for positive, left for negative) on integer line.

edge.name: Perpendicular Bisector Operationalises Reflection Axis
edge.description: The perpendicular bisector constructed in Ch 8 is identical to the mirror line of symmetry in Ch 9.

edge.name: Tables Fluency Prerequisite for Factors and Multiples
edge.description: Prior Grade Prerequisite: Rapid recall of times tables is necessary for identifying factors without tedious trial and error.

edge.name: Tables Fluency Prerequisite for Equivalent Fractions
edge.description: Prior Grade Prerequisite: Multiplying numerator and denominator requires instant multiplication table fluency.

edge.name: Division Intuition Prerequisite for Divisibility Rules
edge.description: Prior Grade Prerequisite: Division as equal grouping is required before learning divisibility shortcuts.

edge.name: Equal Sharing Prerequisite for Unit Fractions
edge.description: Prior Grade Prerequisite: Equal partitioning of a collection or shape is the foundational basis for 1/n fractions.

edge.name: Half/Quarter Intuition Prerequisite for General Fractions
edge.description: Prior Grade Prerequisite: Recognizing 1/2 and 1/4 in concrete objects precedes formal symbolic fraction notation.

edge.name: 2D Shapes Prerequisite for Lines and Angles
edge.description: Prior Grade Prerequisite: Familiarity with polygons precedes formal definitions of point, line, and ray.

edge.name: 2D Shapes Prerequisite for Perimeter
edge.description: Prior Grade Prerequisite: Knowing shape boundaries precedes computing total perimeter.

edge.name: Ruler Measurement Prerequisite for Line Segments
edge.description: Prior Grade Prerequisite: Accurate 0-mark alignment on 15 cm ruler is prerequisite for Class 6 line segment drawing.

edge.name: Ruler Measurement Prerequisite for Compass Construction
edge.description: Prior Grade Prerequisite: Setting compass radius against ruler requires prior ruler reading fluency.

edge.name: Pictographs Prerequisite for Tally Marks & Bar Graphs
edge.description: Prior Grade Prerequisite: Grouping data with symbols in Grade 5 leads directly to tally groups and bar charts in Grade 6.

edge.name: Class 4 Addition/Subtraction Prerequisite for Large Number Operations
edge.description: Prior Grade Prerequisite: Regrouping fluency in 4-digit numbers precedes operations on 6-8 digit numbers.

edge.name: Skip Counting Prerequisite for Number Sequences
edge.description: Prior Grade Prerequisite: Verbal skip counting precedes algebraic sequence pattern recognition.

edge.name: Thermometer Celsius Scale Contextualises Negative Integers
edge.description: Science Context: Sub-zero thermometer readings (-5°C) provide concrete physical grounding for negative numbers.

edge.name: Sea Level Elevation/Depth Contextualises Opposite Integers
edge.description: Geography Context: Height above sea level (+m) and depth below sea level (-m) ground integer signs in real terrain.

edge.name: Sea Level Benchmark Contextualises Zero as Neutral Datum
edge.description: Geography Context: Sea level as exactly 0 meter clarifies why 0 is neither positive nor negative.

edge.name: Rainfall Tracking Contextualises Data Handling in Science
edge.description: Science Context: Environmental rainfall tables demonstrate real-world utility of tally marks and frequency charts.

edge.name: Biological Organisms Contextualise Reflectional Symmetry
edge.description: Biology Context: Butterfly wings and leaf veins show line symmetry evolved in living organisms.

edge.name: Starfish and Flowers Contextualise Radial Symmetry
edge.description: Biology Context: Five-pointed starfish and six-petal flowers demonstrate rotational and multi-axis symmetry.

edge.name: Chemical Dilution Ratios Contextualise Rational Fractions
edge.description: Chemistry Context: 1 part acid in 4 parts water (1/5 total solution) exemplifies proper fraction mixtures.

edge.name: Compass Bearings Contextualise Angles in Physics/Navigation
edge.description: Navigation Context: Navigational bearings (East = 90°, South = 180°) contextualise angles as clockwise rotations.

edge.name: Architectural Tile Tessellations Contextualise Geometric Patterns
edge.description: Art Context: Rangoli and mosaic tiling show mathematical pattern-finding in human culture and heritage.

misconception.name: Extends a sequence by guessing a familiar rule without checking all given terms.
misconception.description: Extends a sequence by guessing a familiar rule without checking all given terms.
misconception.evidence_or_trigger: Proposes a rule that fits only the last pair or misses one of the supplied terms.
misconception.intervention_or_followup: Ask the learner to state the rule and test it against each term before extending.

misconception.name: Confuses odd and even sequences or applies an inconsistent step size.
misconception.description: Confuses odd and even sequences or applies an inconsistent step size.
misconception.evidence_or_trigger: Repeatedly misclassifies or extends odd/even sequences inconsistently.
misconception.intervention_or_followup: Use pairs of counters or a number line; ask what changes from one term to the next.

misconception.name: Relies on memorised number lists without connecting the pattern to its visual arrangement.
misconception.description: Relies on memorised number lists without connecting the pattern to its visual arrangement.
misconception.evidence_or_trigger: Names terms correctly but cannot construct or interpret the corresponding dot arrangement across tasks.
misconception.intervention_or_followup: Build dot triangles and square arrays; ask what is added at each stage.

misconception.name: Adds a fixed number rather than combining the two preceding terms in the Virahanka sequence.
misconception.description: Adds a fixed number rather than combining the two preceding terms in the Virahanka sequence.
misconception.evidence_or_trigger: Repeatedly extends sequence with a constant increment despite prompts to inspect previous terms.
misconception.intervention_or_followup: Mark the two preceding terms for each new term and model their sum.

misconception.name: Adds 2 or 3 instead of multiplying by 2 or 3 in powers sequences.
misconception.description: Adds 2 or 3 instead of multiplying by 2 or 3 in powers sequences.
misconception.evidence_or_trigger: Repeatedly adds a constant difference when asked to extend a powers sequence.
misconception.intervention_or_followup: Compare successive terms using multiplication and repeated grouping.

misconception.name: Recognises odd-number sums as squares in examples but cannot explain the relationship.
misconception.description: Recognises odd-number sums as squares in examples but cannot explain the relationship.
misconception.evidence_or_trigger: Gives a few correct results but cannot connect the added odd-number layer to the growing square representation.
misconception.intervention_or_followup: Build a square array one outer layer at a time and count the new dots.

misconception.name: Counts sides or corners inconsistently when connecting regular polygons to a number sequence.
misconception.description: Counts sides or corners inconsistently when connecting regular polygons to a number sequence.
misconception.evidence_or_trigger: Repeatedly skips or double-counts sides/corners in multiple shapes.
misconception.intervention_or_followup: Mark each side/corner once; record the count beside each shape.

misconception.name: Counts visible components in a shape pattern without a consistent counting strategy.
misconception.description: Counts visible components in a shape pattern without a consistent counting strategy.
misconception.evidence_or_trigger: Repeatedly double-counts or omits lines/components across stages.
misconception.intervention_or_followup: Colour or label each counted component once; compare counts between consecutive stages.

misconception.name: Longer arms mean larger angle
misconception.description: Believes an angle with longer drawn arms is larger than an angle with shorter arms.
misconception.evidence_or_trigger: Selects angle with longer drawn ray segments when comparing openness.
misconception.intervention_or_followup: Overlay transparent angles of equal degree with differing arm lengths to show congruence.

misconception.name: Protractor scale inversion
misconception.description: Reads wrong scale on protractor (e.g., reading 60 deg instead of 120 deg for an obtuse angle).
misconception.evidence_or_trigger: Consistently reads supplementary angle value because of reading from wrong 0-line.
misconception.intervention_or_followup: Anchor angle type visually as acute (<90) or obtuse (>90) before reading numerical scale.

misconception.name: Confuses ray with finite segment
misconception.description: Treats ray as finite because of fixed paper length; fails to understand infinite extension.
misconception.evidence_or_trigger: States a ray has two endpoints or a fixed length.
misconception.intervention_or_followup: Demonstrate laser pointer or torch beam analogy from source to infinity.

misconception.name: Orientation dependency in angle classification
misconception.description: Fails to recognize right or acute angle when rotated into non-horizontal orientation.
misconception.evidence_or_trigger: Classifies non-horizontal right angle as obtuse or acute depending on tilt.
misconception.intervention_or_followup: Rotate paper or use square corner template to test orientation invariance.

misconception.name: Leading zero in smallest number
misconception.description: Places 0 as the leading digit when forming smallest number (e.g., writing 0357 instead of 3057 as a 4-digit number).
misconception.evidence_or_trigger: Writes a number with fewer significant digits than required due to leading zero.
misconception.intervention_or_followup: Explain that leading zero does not contribute place value; place smallest non-zero digit first, then zero.

misconception.name: Midpoint rounding down
misconception.description: Rounds down when the last digit is exactly 5 (e.g., rounding 45 to 40 instead of 50).
misconception.evidence_or_trigger: Inconsistently rounds 5 down or fails to apply conventional upward midpoint rounding.
misconception.intervention_or_followup: Use number line to show 5 is exactly midway and convention directs to higher ten.

misconception.name: Period comma confusion across systems
misconception.description: Applies International comma groups (3-3) to Indian Lakhs/Crores or vice-versa.
misconception.evidence_or_trigger: Misreads 10,00,000 as 1 million without understanding period equivalence.
misconception.intervention_or_followup: Use dual-row place value chart to compare periods directly.

misconception.name: Ignoring pictograph key/scale
misconception.description: Counts each pictograph icon as 1 unit, ignoring the scale key (e.g., counting 4 icons as 4 instead of 40).
misconception.evidence_or_trigger: Multiplies icon count by 1 instead of scale value.
misconception.intervention_or_followup: Circle the key prominently; write the value above each icon before adding.

misconception.name: Non-uniform bar width or spacing
misconception.description: Draws bars of varying widths or inconsistent spacing, distorting visual area perception.
misconception.evidence_or_trigger: Varies bar width between categories.
misconception.intervention_or_followup: Use grid paper and count exact grid squares for bar widths and gaps.

misconception.name: Misreading in-between values on coarse scales
misconception.description: Fails to interpolate between major grid lines (e.g. reading a height midway between 20 and 30 as 21).
misconception.evidence_or_trigger: Guesses single digits rather than proportional midpoint.
misconception.intervention_or_followup: Subdivide axis unit interval with tick marks to estimate proportional values.

misconception.name: 1 is prime misconception
misconception.description: Classifies 1 as a prime number because it is divisible by 1 and itself.
misconception.evidence_or_trigger: States 1 is prime, failing to apply the requirement of exactly two distinct factors.
misconception.intervention_or_followup: Write factors of 1 (only {1}) and factors of 2 ({1, 2}); emphasize prime requires two different factors.

misconception.name: All odd numbers are prime
misconception.description: Believes odd numbers are synonymous with prime numbers (e.g. classifying 9, 15, 21 as prime).
misconception.evidence_or_trigger: Classifies composite odd numbers as prime without testing divisibility by 3, 5, 7.
misconception.intervention_or_followup: Use arrays or counters to show 9 forms a 3x3 square and 15 forms 3x5 rectangle.

misconception.name: Co-primes must be prime numbers
misconception.description: Believes numbers in a co-prime pair must themselves be prime numbers.
misconception.evidence_or_trigger: Rejects pairs like (8, 9) or (4, 15) as co-prime because individual numbers are composite.
misconception.intervention_or_followup: List factors of 8 ({1,2,4,8}) and 9 ({1,3,9}); circle common factor 1 to demonstrate co-primality.

misconception.name: Confusing factors and multiples
misconception.description: Reverses terms factor and multiple (e.g., stating 24 is a factor of 6).
misconception.evidence_or_trigger: States a larger number is a factor of a smaller number.
misconception.intervention_or_followup: Use linguistic anchor: Factors divide (smaller/equal), Multiples multiply (larger/equal).

misconception.name: Confusing perimeter and area units
misconception.description: Writes linear units (cm) for area or square units (cm^2) for perimeter.
misconception.evidence_or_trigger: States area is in cm or perimeter is in cm^2.
misconception.intervention_or_followup: Trace boundary with string (1D line, cm); fill surface with 1x1 tiles (2D squares, cm^2).

misconception.name: Constant perimeter implies constant area fallacy
misconception.description: Believes shapes with equal perimeter must enclose the same area.
misconception.evidence_or_trigger: Predicts rectangles with perimeter 20 cm (e.g. 9x1 vs 5x5) have equal area.
misconception.intervention_or_followup: Use fixed loop of string to make different rectangles and count grid squares inside.

misconception.name: Including internal edges in compound perimeter
misconception.description: Sums all segment lengths including internal dividing lines when finding perimeter of combined shapes.
misconception.evidence_or_trigger: Adds internal shared boundary into total perimeter.
misconception.intervention_or_followup: Walk a toy figure along only the outside perimeter fence to trace path.

misconception.name: Slant height used instead of perpendicular height in triangle area
misconception.description: Multiplies side length instead of perpendicular height when computing triangle area.
misconception.evidence_or_trigger: Uses non-perpendicular slant edge in 1/2 * b * h formula.
misconception.intervention_or_followup: Draw perpendicular altitude with right-angle symbol; compare with box enclosing triangle.

misconception.name: Direct addition of denominators (across-adding)
misconception.description: Adds numerators and denominators straight across: a/b + c/d = (a+c)/(b+d) (e.g. 1/3 + 2/5 = 3/8).
misconception.evidence_or_trigger: Consistently calculates sum of numerators over sum of denominators on unlike fraction items.
misconception.intervention_or_followup: Visual fraction strip overlay: show 1/3 and 2/5 have different slice widths; cannot sum until cut into matching 15ths.

misconception.name: Larger denominator means larger value misconception
misconception.description: Believes 1/8 is larger than 1/4 because 8 > 4 (transferring whole number ordering intuition).
misconception.evidence_or_trigger: States fraction with greater denominator is larger when numerators are equal.
misconception.intervention_or_followup: Pizza sharing model: sharing 1 pizza among 8 people yields smaller individual slices than among 4.

misconception.name: Unequal partition counting error
misconception.description: Counts shaded parts without ensuring all partition parts are of equal size.
misconception.evidence_or_trigger: Labels a shape with unequal parts (e.g. 1 shaded out of 3 unequal sections) as 1/3.
misconception.intervention_or_followup: Provide partitioned figures with unequal areas; ask student to verify congruence before counting.

misconception.name: Partial scaling in equivalent fractions
misconception.description: Multiplies only the numerator or only the denominator when attempting to find equivalent fraction.
misconception.evidence_or_trigger: Scales top by 3 but leaves bottom unchanged (e.g., 2/5 = 6/5).
misconception.intervention_or_followup: Golden rule of fractions: scaling must be multiplying by (k/k = 1), so top and bottom get identical multiplier.

misconception.name: Compass needle slipping or radius alteration
misconception.description: Alters compass aperture during drawing, creating distorted circular arcs.
misconception.evidence_or_trigger: Arcs fail to intersect at accurate equidistant points due to loose compass joint.
misconception.intervention_or_followup: Tighten compass screw; anchor needle firmly on paper; rotate only the pencil arm from the top knob.

misconception.name: Radius vs diameter confusion in compass setting
misconception.description: Sets compass opening to diameter length instead of radius when asked to draw a circle of given diameter.
misconception.evidence_or_trigger: Draws circle with double the requested size.
misconception.intervention_or_followup: Highlight that compass opening always equals radius (half of diameter).

misconception.name: Ruler measurement from 1 instead of 0
misconception.description: Aligns start of line segment with 1 cm mark instead of 0 cm line on ruler.
misconception.evidence_or_trigger: Constructed segment is exactly 1 cm shorter than required.
misconception.intervention_or_followup: Place zero line mark with a red pencil dot before drawing.

misconception.name: Rectangle diagonal symmetry fallacy
misconception.description: Believes the diagonal of any rectangle is a line of symmetry.
misconception.evidence_or_trigger: States a non-square rectangle has 4 lines of symmetry by including both diagonals.
misconception.intervention_or_followup: Fold a rectangular paper along its diagonal: show that the two halves do not coincide.

misconception.name: Translation instead of reflection
misconception.description: Draws the missing half by sliding (translating) the shape rather than flipping (reflecting) it.
misconception.evidence_or_trigger: Copies shape facing same direction rather than mirror-inverted.
misconception.intervention_or_followup: Place a small vertical mirror on the symmetry line to observe true mirror reflection.

misconception.name: Equating vertices with rotational order
misconception.description: Assumes a shape with n vertices always has rotational symmetry order n (e.g. parallelogram has 4 vertices but only order 2).
misconception.evidence_or_trigger: Assigns order 4 to a non-rhombic parallelogram.
misconception.intervention_or_followup: Rotate tracing paper on top of shape; count matching fits across a full 360-degree circle.

misconception.name: Larger absolute value means greater negative integer
misconception.description: Believes -8 is greater than -2 because 8 > 2 (failing to understand distance to the left of zero).
misconception.evidence_or_trigger: Selects -8 > -2 or orders negative integers in reverse order.
misconception.intervention_or_followup: Number line temperature analogy: -8 deg C is colder (lower) than -2 deg C.

misconception.name: Overgeneralising two negatives make positive to addition
misconception.description: Calculates (-3) + (-5) = +8 instead of -8 by overapplying multiplication double-negative rule to addition.
misconception.evidence_or_trigger: Produces positive sum when adding two negative integers.
misconception.intervention_or_followup: Debt model: owing 3 rupees and owing 5 rupees means owing 8 rupees total (-8), not gaining wealth.

misconception.name: Negative predecessor whole number reversal
misconception.description: States predecessor of -4 is -3 instead of -5 (transferring positive number predecessor logic).
misconception.evidence_or_trigger: Reverses direction of predecessor on negative side of number line.
misconception.intervention_or_followup: Predecessor is always 1 step to the left on the number line; -5 is to the left of -4.

misconception.name: Subtracting negative treated as simple subtraction
misconception.description: Evaluates 5 - (-3) as 5 - 3 = 2 instead of 5 + 3 = 8.
misconception.evidence_or_trigger: Ignores the negative sign inside the parenthesis during subtraction.
misconception.intervention_or_followup: Token model: taking away 3 negative tokens requires adding 3 zero pairs, leaving 3 extra positives (+8).

assessment.name: sequence extension + rule explanation
assessment.description: Extend a number sequence by three terms and state the rule in words.
assessment.evidence_or_trigger: Accuracy, rule consistency across all given terms, explanation.
assessment.intervention_or_followup: Do not score the next term alone as evidence of mastery.

assessment.name: visual construction
assessment.description: Build or draw a triangular-number or square-number arrangement and label its count.
assessment.evidence_or_trigger: Mapping between visual arrangement and numerical term.
assessment.intervention_or_followup: Do not penalise drawing neatness when the mathematical relation is clear.

assessment.name: compare rules
assessment.description: Choose and explain the rule that fits a sequence, then extend it.
assessment.evidence_or_trigger: Distinguishes previous-two-term rule from repeated multiplication.
assessment.intervention_or_followup: Use more than one sequence to reduce chance guessing.

assessment.name: pattern justification
assessment.description: Explain why the first few odd-number sums match square numbers, using a picture or words.
assessment.evidence_or_trigger: Connects new odd-number layer to a growing square.
assessment.intervention_or_followup: A memorised formula without explanation is partial evidence only.

assessment.name: shape-sequence continuation
assessment.description: Continue a regular-polygon sequence and record side/corner counts.
assessment.evidence_or_trigger: Correct shape order and count mapping.
assessment.intervention_or_followup: Ensure shape diagrams are legible and not misleadingly scaled.

assessment.name: component count + rule
assessment.description: Count lines, small squares, triangles or line segments across consecutive figures and describe the rule.
assessment.evidence_or_trigger: Systematic counting and valid relation to sequence.
assessment.intervention_or_followup: Do not confuse a visual counting slip with a confirmed misconception.

assessment.name: transfer task
assessment.description: Find a relationship between a number sequence and a shape sequence and explain it.
assessment.evidence_or_trigger: Learner connects representations and justifies the relationship.
assessment.intervention_or_followup: Accept multiple valid explanations when supported by evidence.

assessment.name: geometric entities identification
assessment.description: Differentiate between points, lines, segments, and rays from symbolic and visual diagrams.
assessment.evidence_or_trigger: Correct identification across multiple orientations.
assessment.intervention_or_followup: Ensure arrowheads and endpoint dots are clearly drawn.

assessment.name: angle type classification
assessment.description: Classify angles as acute, right, obtuse, straight, or reflex without protractor measurement.
assessment.evidence_or_trigger: Accurate benchmark classification relative to 90 and 180 degrees.
assessment.intervention_or_followup: Include rotated orientations to rule out orientation bias.

assessment.name: protractor reading and drawing
assessment.description: Measure given angles and construct angles to target degree values.
assessment.evidence_or_trigger: Measurement within +/- 1 degree accuracy; correct scale selection.
assessment.intervention_or_followup: Verify alignment with zero-line and center-cross of protractor.

assessment.name: place value and large numbers
assessment.description: Write numbers in expanded form and place commas according to Indian and International conventions.
assessment.evidence_or_trigger: Accurate period grouping and word naming.
assessment.intervention_or_followup: Test numbers with interior zeros.

assessment.name: digit arrangement and estimation
assessment.description: Create extreme numbers from given digits and estimate answers to multi-digit operations.
assessment.evidence_or_trigger: Valid non-zero leading digits and reasonable estimation range.
assessment.intervention_or_followup: Check mental estimation vs exact calculation.

assessment.name: pictograph reading with key
assessment.description: Read and extract values from a pictograph featuring whole and half symbols.
assessment.evidence_or_trigger: Correct application of scale multiplier to both complete and partial symbols.
assessment.intervention_or_followup: Do not use unit scale 1:1 for this diagnostic.

assessment.name: bar graph construction
assessment.description: Construct a complete bar graph from a frequency table on grid paper.
assessment.evidence_or_trigger: Appropriate scale, uniform bar widths, equal spacing, and accurate labels.
assessment.intervention_or_followup: Check scale starts at zero.

assessment.name: prime and composite classification
assessment.description: Classify numbers from 1 to 50 as prime, composite, or neither.
assessment.evidence_or_trigger: Accurate identification of 1 as neither and 2 as even prime.

assessment.name: HCF and LCM prime factorisation
assessment.description: Find HCF and LCM of number pairs using prime factor trees or division.
assessment.evidence_or_trigger: Correct prime decomposition and valid power product extraction.
assessment.intervention_or_followup: Ensure student does not multiply HCF and LCM blindly.

assessment.name: divisibility rule verification
assessment.description: Determine divisibility of large numbers by 3, 4, 6, 8, 9, 11 without long division.
assessment.evidence_or_trigger: Correct explanation of digit sum or end digit criteria.
assessment.intervention_or_followup: Use numbers with interior zeros.

assessment.name: perimeter and area calculation
assessment.description: Calculate perimeter and area of rectangles, squares, and compound shapes with correct units.
assessment.evidence_or_trigger: Accurate formula application and distinct linear vs square units.
assessment.intervention_or_followup: Include composite shapes with missing side lengths.

assessment.name: perimeter vs area discrimination task
assessment.description: Classify real-world word problems as requiring perimeter versus area calculations.
assessment.evidence_or_trigger: Correct conceptual assignment and numerical resolution.
assessment.intervention_or_followup: Include word problems with distractors.

assessment.name: unlike fraction addition diagnostic
assessment.description: Evaluate addition of unlike fractions (e.g., 1/3 + 2/5) requiring LCM finding.
assessment.evidence_or_trigger: Detects presence of direct addition slip (3/8) vs LCM conversion (11/15).
assessment.intervention_or_followup: Engineered distractor option must include (a+c)/(b+d).

assessment.name: equivalent fractions and simplification
assessment.description: Generate equivalent fractions and reduce fractions to simplest form.
assessment.evidence_or_trigger: Division by HCF; verification of co-prime final terms.
assessment.intervention_or_followup: Include fractions with non-obvious common factors like 14/21 or 12/16.

assessment.name: number line fraction placement
assessment.description: Plot and label proper, improper, and mixed fractions on a continuous number line.
assessment.evidence_or_trigger: Accurate subdivision of unit intervals; positioning improper fractions beyond 1.
assessment.intervention_or_followup: Avoid pre-marked tick marks.

assessment.name: perpendicular bisector construction
assessment.description: Construct the perpendicular bisector of a given line segment using compass and straightedge.
assessment.evidence_or_trigger: Arcs clearly visible, intersection line orthogonal to segment and passing through midpoint.
assessment.intervention_or_followup: Do not erase construction arcs.

assessment.name: circle drawing and diagonal verification
assessment.description: Construct a rectangle and measure diagonals to verify equality.
assessment.evidence_or_trigger: Measurement precision within 1 mm.
assessment.intervention_or_followup: Verify sharp pencil and accurate ruler alignment.

assessment.name: lines of symmetry counting
assessment.description: Identify and draw all lines of symmetry on plane figures including polygons and letters.
assessment.evidence_or_trigger: Correct identification; absence of false diagonal symmetry on rectangles.
assessment.intervention_or_followup: Include scalene triangle, rectangle, and square.

assessment.name: rotational symmetry order determination
assessment.description: Determine the angle and order of rotational symmetry for regular and non-regular polygons.
assessment.evidence_or_trigger: Correct order calculation (e.g. order 2 for rectangle, order 4 for square).
assessment.intervention_or_followup: Ensure center of rotation is marked.

assessment.name: integer comparison and ordering
assessment.description: Order a mixed set of positive and negative integers from least to greatest.
assessment.evidence_or_trigger: Correct placement of negative integers with larger numerals as lowest values.

assessment.name: integer addition and subtraction
assessment.description: Evaluate addition and subtraction expressions involving like and unlike signs.
assessment.evidence_or_trigger: Accurate resolution of double negatives and unlike sign additions.

intervention.name: PAT-02
intervention.description: Give a short sequence on paper. Ask the learner to circle the change between terms, write the rule in words, test every given term, then extend by three terms.
intervention.evidence_or_trigger: Rule fits all given terms and correctly generates new terms on a fresh example.
intervention.intervention_or_followup: Give a short sequence on paper. Ask the learner to circle the change between terms, write the rule in words, test every given term, then extend by three terms.

intervention.name: PAT-07/PAT-08
intervention.description: Use counters or drawn dots to build the first few triangular and square arrangements. Add one stage at a time and record the count beneath each figure.
intervention.evidence_or_trigger: Learner maps each arrangement to its number and explains what was added.
intervention.intervention_or_followup: Use counters or drawn dots to build the first few triangular and square arrangements. Add one stage at a time and record the count beneath each figure.

intervention.name: PAT-10
intervention.description: Write the two previous terms above a blank term and physically add them; repeat across several terms, then fade the scaffolding.
intervention.evidence_or_trigger: Learner explains and independently applies the previous-two-terms rule.
intervention.intervention_or_followup: Write the two previous terms above a blank term and physically add them; repeat across several terms, then fade the scaffolding.

intervention.name: PAT-11/PAT-12
intervention.description: Create repeated groups or multiplication arrows between terms; compare multiplying by a fixed factor with adding a fixed amount.
intervention.evidence_or_trigger: Learner distinguishes multiplicative pattern from constant-difference pattern.
intervention.intervention_or_followup: Create repeated groups or multiplication arrows between terms; compare multiplying by a fixed factor with adding a fixed amount.

intervention.name: PAT-16
intervention.description: Build a square of counters. Add the next odd-number layer in a different mark or colour and count the new counters.
intervention.evidence_or_trigger: Learner explains how each next odd number completes the next square.
intervention.intervention_or_followup: Build a square of counters. Add the next odd-number layer in a different mark or colour and count the new counters.

intervention.name: PAT-19/PAT-24
intervention.description: Label sides and corners one by one on a sequence of polygons, then make a two-column shape/count table.
intervention.evidence_or_trigger: Accurately relates shape names to side/corner counts on new examples.
intervention.intervention_or_followup: Label sides and corners one by one on a sequence of polygons, then make a two-column shape/count table.

intervention.name: PAT-20/PAT-21/PAT-22/PAT-23
intervention.description: Use a systematic count: number each line/component once, record the total for each stage, and compare stage-to-stage changes.
intervention.evidence_or_trigger: Learner counts consistently and states a defensible rule.
intervention.intervention_or_followup: Use a systematic count: number each line/component once, record the total for each stage, and compare stage-to-stage changes.

intervention.name: LIN-09/LIN-12
intervention.description: Use two hinged cardboard strips to explore angle as amount of turn; trim one strip to prove length does not change angle openness.
intervention.evidence_or_trigger: Learner explains that angle measure depends on rotation, not arm length.
intervention.intervention_or_followup: Hinged paper strips turn activity.

intervention.name: LIN-19
intervention.description: Color-code the base arm and circle the corresponding 0-degree baseline on protractor before tracing degrees upward.
intervention.evidence_or_trigger: Learner correctly chooses the scale starting at 0 on the base arm.
intervention.intervention_or_followup: Dual-color baseline protractor tracing.

intervention.name: NUM-04
intervention.description: Use physical digit cards including a 0 card. Challenge student to make a 4-digit number and verify that a 3-digit reading invalidates leading zero.
intervention.evidence_or_trigger: Student correctly places 0 in second place value slot.
intervention.intervention_or_followup: Physical digit card arrangement.

intervention.name: DAT-05
intervention.description: Provide pictograph worksheet where student must write the scale value on every symbol before calculating category totals.
intervention.evidence_or_trigger: Student consistently multiplies symbol count by scale.
intervention.intervention_or_followup: Annotation of symbol values on pictographs.

intervention.name: PRM-07
intervention.description: Use rectangular array counters: any number of counters that can form a rectangle with width > 1 is composite; numbers forming only a 1-wide strip are prime.
intervention.evidence_or_trigger: Learner explains prime as forming only 1 x n line array.
intervention.intervention_or_followup: Array rectangle formation with unit counters.

intervention.name: PRM-11
intervention.description: Venn diagram factor sorting: draw two overlapping circles for factors of two composite numbers; observe that only 1 sits in the intersection.
intervention.evidence_or_trigger: Learner confirms (8, 9) have only 1 in intersection and explains co-primality.
intervention.intervention_or_followup: Venn diagram factor intersection.

intervention.name: PER-15
intervention.description: Fixed-perimeter string activity: take a 24 cm loop of string. Form rectangles: 11x1 (area 11), 10x2 (area 20), 8x4 (area 32), 6x6 (area 36). Record in table to show area changes drastically.
intervention.evidence_or_trigger: Learner explains that perimeter measures outer rope length while area measures enclosed space.
intervention.intervention_or_followup: Fixed-perimeter loop exploration.

intervention.name: FRC-17
intervention.description: Interactive fraction strip manipulatives: place 1/3 strip and 2/5 strip side-by-side. Slide 1/15 strips underneath to prove 5/15 + 6/15 = 11/15.
intervention.evidence_or_trigger: Learner explains why unlike denominators cannot be added directly without finding equal slice subdivisions.
intervention.intervention_or_followup: Visual fraction strip alignment and LCD conversion.

intervention.name: FRC-10
intervention.description: Folding paper strips: fold a strip into 3 equal parts (1/3). Fold each part in half to get 6 parts (2/6); fold again to get 12 parts (4/12).
intervention.evidence_or_trigger: Learner observes shaded amount remains unchanged while number of pieces increases proportionally.
intervention.intervention_or_followup: Paper folding equivalent fraction demonstration.

intervention.name: CON-13
intervention.description: Paper folding symmetry: draw segment AB on translucent paper. Fold paper so point A falls exactly onto point B. Unfold: crease is the perpendicular bisector.
intervention.evidence_or_trigger: Learner connects the folded crease to the equidistant arc intersection line.
intervention.intervention_or_followup: Paper folding symmetry bisector.

intervention.name: SYM-02/SYM-05
intervention.description: Rectangle diagonal folding test: give student index card. Have student fold on diagonal. Note the protruding flaps. Fold along vertical/horizontal midlines: note perfect coincidence.
intervention.evidence_or_trigger: Learner explains why diagonal is not a line of symmetry in non-square rectangles.
intervention.intervention_or_followup: Tangible paper folding diagnostic.

intervention.name: INT-07
intervention.description: Vertical thermometer ladder: draw vertical number line from +10 down to -10. Place markers for temperatures. Higher on ladder = warmer = greater.
intervention.evidence_or_trigger: Learner points to -2 being higher on ladder than -8, confirming -2 > -8.
intervention.intervention_or_followup: Vertical temperature line placement.

intervention.name: INT-10/INT-14/INT-15
intervention.description: Red and black two-color counter chips: black = +1, red = -1. For 5 - (-3): lay out 5 black chips. Need to remove 3 red chips. Add 3 zero pairs (3 black + 3 red). Now remove 3 red chips: 8 black chips remain.
intervention.evidence_or_trigger: Learner physically manipulates zero pairs to understand double negative removal.
intervention.intervention_or_followup: Zero pair chip manipulation.

mastery_rule.name: PAT-02
mastery_rule.description: Provisional mastery when learner extends at least two different sequences, states a rule fitting every supplied term, and verifies the rule on a new term.

mastery_rule.name: PAT-07/PAT-08/PAT-09
mastery_rule.description: Provisional mastery when learner correctly maps number term to visual arrangement and explains the relationship on at least two examples.

mastery_rule.name: PAT-10/PAT-11/PAT-12
mastery_rule.description: Provisional mastery when learner identifies the generating rule and applies it to multiple unseen terms across the relevant sequence type.
mastery_rule.status: Proposed; do not generalise across all sequences automatically.

mastery_rule.name: PAT-16
mastery_rule.description: Provisional mastery when learner explains the odd-number/square relationship with a diagram or coherent reasoning, not only recalled results.

mastery_rule.name: PAT-18/PAT-19/PAT-24
mastery_rule.description: Provisional mastery when learner continues a shape sequence and correctly connects shape features to number counts with an explanation.

mastery_rule.name: PAT-20/PAT-21/PAT-22/PAT-23
mastery_rule.description: Provisional mastery when learner systematically counts components across stages and explains the resulting sequence.
mastery_rule.status: Proposed; evaluate each shape sequence separately.

mastery_rule.name: LIN-01/LIN-02/LIN-03/LIN-04
mastery_rule.description: Provisional mastery when learner correctly identifies, names, and draws lines, segments, and rays across 3 distinct tasks.

mastery_rule.name: LIN-13/LIN-16/LIN-17/LIN-18
mastery_rule.description: Provisional mastery when learner correctly classifies acute, right, obtuse, and reflex angles across varying orientations.

mastery_rule.name: LIN-19/LIN-20
mastery_rule.description: Provisional mastery when learner measures and draws angles within 2 degrees of target across both left-opening and right-opening configurations.

mastery_rule.name: NUM-01/NUM-04
mastery_rule.description: Provisional mastery when learner accurately writes, reads, and forms extreme numbers across both Indian and International systems.

mastery_rule.name: DAT-05/DAT-06/DAT-11
mastery_rule.description: Provisional mastery when learner correctly interprets both pictographs (with scale > 1) and bar graphs across 3 distinct datasets.

mastery_rule.name: PRM-07/PRM-11
mastery_rule.description: Provisional mastery when learner correctly classifies primes/composites and identifies co-prime composite pairs with justification.
mastery_rule.status: Proposed; test with odd composites like 27 and 35.

mastery_rule.name: PRM-15/PRM-16
mastery_rule.description: Provisional mastery when learner computes both HCF and LCM via prime factorisation for 3 distinct number pairs.

mastery_rule.name: PER-03/PER-10/PER-15
mastery_rule.description: Provisional mastery when learner accurately calculates perimeter and area across regular and compound shapes and explains why equal perimeter does not guarantee equal area.

mastery_rule.name: FRC-10/FRC-17
mastery_rule.description: Provisional mastery when learner correctly converts to equivalent fractions and adds/subtracts unlike fractions with 0 occurrences of direct denominator addition across 4 distinct items.

mastery_rule.name: CON-02/CON-13
mastery_rule.description: Provisional mastery when learner constructs accurate circles and perpendicular bisectors with intact construction arcs across 2 separate tasks.
mastery_rule.status: Proposed; teacher inspection of construction lines.

mastery_rule.name: SYM-02/SYM-06/SYM-12
mastery_rule.description: Provisional mastery when learner correctly identifies reflection lines and rotational orders across diverse 2D shapes without diagonal rectangle error.
mastery_rule.status: Proposed; test with rectangles and kites.

mastery_rule.name: INT-07/INT-10/INT-11/INT-15
mastery_rule.description: Provisional mastery when learner correctly orders integers and evaluates addition/subtraction without double-negative or like-sign confusion across 5 distinct expressions.
